one_month_reasoning: The main event in the window is the fiscal Q1 FY27 report. No date had been announced by 2026-10-02, but past dates (2023-10-26, 2024-10-22, 2025-10-28) put it inside the window with about 90% probability. Guidance is $4.1B +/- $0.1B revenue and $7.30 +/- $0.20 non-GAAP EPS, with about 50% operating margin and 231M diluted shares. Management says revenue and margin will grow every quarter through FY27, and pricing for CY2027 is already contracted, so a beat and a higher Q2 guide are likely. The stock will move on two other things: what management says about CY2028 contract pricing, and how it answers the 2026-10-02 Nikkei/Toshiba report. The July print shows the reaction can go either way (-8.5% on the day, then +14% over the next two days). The insider-selling overhang I cited in round 1 turned out to be mostly tax sell-to-cover, so I removed it, but it was never a 1-month driver. Net: median about flat ($836), with a sigma of about 22%, slightly above the 0.75/3.5 = 21% monthly vol because earnings fall inside the window.

fair_value.method: Blend of 18x my NTM EPS at Oct-2027 (~$43, a probability-weighted average of three CY2028 pricing cases) plus ~$6/share net cash = $780 (60%), and a 4.5% FCF yield on ~$36.5 FCF/share (85% conversion, 230M shares) plus net cash = $817 (40%). Result: about $795, ~5% below spot. Gross debt is ~$2.4B after the July and September retirements.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS at Oct-2027 ~$43 (FY28 ~$42 weighted across CY2028 price-per-EB cases -5% / flat / +10% at 30/35/35%) x 18x + ~$6/share net cash

inputs_detail.derivation: Q1 guide of $7.30, then the sequential revenue and margin growth management guides for every FY27 quarter: about 7.3 / 8.0 / 8.6 / 9.2. This is the low half of the $33-36 range, because the Q4 call says part of the September price-per-exabyte jump was a one-off: an initial HAMR customer's preferential pricing rolled off.

inputs_detail.value: Volume mostly allocated into CY2028; pricing contracted for all of CY2027 only

inputs_detail.derivation: Before this cycle, management guided price/EB growth of mid-to-high single digits a year. June was +10% YoY and the September guide implies about +20%. Toshiba's ~¥60B doubling (by Mar-2028; MAMR-only until HAMR mass production in Toshiba FY2028) is aimed exactly at the CY2028 negotiation window. As the skeptic I put 30% on the price per EB falling: three suppliers with one doubling capacity is the classic start of a cycle turn.

H1 FY28 (Jul-Dec 2027) runs on CY2027 contract pricing plus about 5% quarterly volume growth (EPS ~9.6, ~10.0). H2 FY28 reprices: -5% per EB costs about 10% of EPS at a ~53-55% gross margin, flat holds the run-rate, and +10% adds about 12%. NTM at Oct-2027 is one quarter further out than FY28, so add about $1.

The stock reached about 40x forward at the July peak and is about 25x FY27 today, against a 10-15x HDD history. 18x sits above history because volumes are allocated into 2028, but below today because CY2028 pricing is open and Toshiba is adding supply into that window.

inputs_detail.input: Net cash per share at horizon
inputs_detail.derivation: Gross debt was $3.6B at FY26 end, less $1.2B retired in the September quarter ($1.0B HY in July, exchangeables on 2026-09-08), leaving ~$2.4B. Q1-Q4 FY27 FCF of over $6B, less buybacks and dividends, leaves modest net cash; I assume a large share goes to buybacks.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM FCF ~$8.4B / 230M diluted shares = ~$36.5/share at a 4.5% yield = $811, plus ~$6 net cash

inputs_detail.value: 4.7% of FY26 revenue; FY27 within the 4-6% target

inputs_detail.derivation: Q1 guide of 231M includes ~2M of exchangeable dilution that ended on 2026-09-08 (1.65M shares issued). Buybacks roughly offset equity compensation.
FY26 FCF of $3.1B on about $3.5B non-GAAP net income is about 0.87-0.88. I trim it slightly for working capital as revenue grows.

Investment-grade (Fitch BBB-) cyclical hardware at likely peak margins, with CY2028 pricing open. Today's yield is ~3%; I use a premium of about 1.5 points, between my round-1 3.5% and the 5-6% others used.

bear.story: The supply response lands in the CY2028 negotiation. Toshiba's doubling (plus WDC ePMR/HAMR additions) and some hyperscaler digestion in late 2027 push new-LTA price per EB down, and the market looks through H1 FY28 to falling FY29 EPS. NTM EPS of about $35 at 13x, near the top of the HDD cyclical range. STX's own history (-44% in 2018, -60% in 2022 from cycle peaks) shows this path is ordinary for the name, though in those cycles pricing had already rolled over.

base.story: FY27 EPS is about $33-34, delivered with sequential beats. CY2028 pricing settles roughly flat to slightly up as Toshiba's MAMR capacity adds only a few % to industry exabytes by end-2027. NTM EPS is about $43-45 at 18x, so the multiple de-rates while earnings grow.

bull.story: AI inference and data retention keep exabyte demand above the mid-20s, Mozaic 4/5 widen the cost/density lead, and CY2028 LTAs reprice up about 10% or more. NTM EPS is about $50 or more and the market keeps a 26-27x growth multiple.

thesis_break_reason: About $510 (-39%) is roughly 12x my ~$43 NTM EPS, at the HDD peak-cycle multiple range. Below it the market would be pricing an actual break in CY2028 contract pricing (flat-to-down price per EB in new LTAs, hyperscaler build-to-order deferrals, a Mozaic 4/5 slip or share loss) rather than 70%-vol noise. The 2026 one-day sector shocks bottomed around $700-750.

reasoning: Round 2. I take the supervisor's fact-checks as established and verified the two that matter most to me against primaries. (1) The Q4 FY26 call transcript, which I opened: 'the vast majority of our nearline exabytes are now allocated into calendar 2028', pricing terms cover 'the entirety of calendar 2027', management is 'confident in delivering sequential revenue growth and margin expansion through fiscal 2027', $1.2B of debt is retired in the September quarter, and the CFO says the preferential-price HAMR volume was 'minimal'. (2) The CEO's 2026-09-15 Form 4: 97,889 shares sold at $772 out of 177,000 vested PSUs, footnoted as issuer-mandated sell-to-cover for tax, with 378k shares still held. So I drop insider selling as bear evidence, and the Kavout '$120M' claim with it. I accept that my round-1 FY28 EPS of $37 was effectively a flat-pricing bear case. I rebuilt it from an explicit CY2028 price-per-EB distribution (-5% / flat / +10% at 30/35/35) on mid-20s exabyte growth, giving NTM EPS of about $43. That is below the supervisor's $47: I keep a skeptic's 30% weight on a pricing decline, because Toshiba's doubling (finished by Mar-2028) lands exactly in the CY2028 negotiation window and part of the September price jump was a one-off. Share count is now 230M and debt is about $2.4B, worth a few dollars per share. Fair value moves from $775 to about $795 (18x NTM EPS with a 4.5% FCF yield), still ~5% below spot. The skeptic case remains the multiple: a three-player oligopoly at peak margins, 25x FY27, with STX's own -44% and -60% post-peak drawdowns as the base rate. For the ladder I used a lognormal with median ~$808 (up from ~$790) and sigma ~0.62, below the 75% realized vol, fattened slightly in the far left tail for a cyclical bust. Scenario mean is ~$858. P(>= spot) is 0.476, up from 0.46. Research this round was tight: 2 fetches and 1 search. The search for a fresh post-Toshiba downgrade found only stale items, so I found no new bear evidence beyond the Toshiba report.
